gap: No result ChatGPT got states that its long-run pick, the OREI EX-230UHD HDBaseT extender (shown at $149.99 as reaching 230 ft 'with 4K support'), only reaches 230 ft at 1080p: OREI's own support page limits 4K@60Hz to 131 ft (40 m) over CAT6 and says it does not support 4K@120Hz, while the short passive 48 Gbps extensions ChatGPT recommended sell for $12.59–$19.99 on Amazon.
standout_why: I compared the cited Cable Matters page, the cited iTechGuides guide and the top-ranked Shinforce list. Cable Matters' page shows a blank 'Price:' field. iTechGuides gives Amazon prices for five short no-name extensions but none for UGREEN, Cable Matters, Monoprice or OREI. Its only HDBaseT figure is for a C2G unit (4K/30 4:4:4 or 4K/60 4:2:0 to about 230 ft). Shinforce shows no prices at all ('Check Price' links only). None of these pages mentions the OREI unit, its 131 ft limit at 4K60, or that it can't do 4K120. The cited Bestways UGREEN HD151 page returned HTTP 429, so I couldn't read it.
decides: This confirms passive 48 Gbps extensions (UGREEN, Cable Matters, Silkland, $12.59–$19.99) for runs of 1–6 ft. It overturns ChatGPT's third pick for anyone who wants 4K over a long run: the OREI unit stops at 131 ft for 4K60 and can't carry 4K120 at any distance. A long 4K120 gaming run needs a certified fiber (AOC) cable such as the Monoprice one ChatGPT showed at $120.04 at Walmart instead.
